lead: # `bsc_base_dir` — so the CLI and the app share ONE on-disk response cache rather than each
# keeping its own and re-fetching what the other already validated.
# The shared CLI scaffold: `bsc github` is the surface without which this crate stays
# linked-but-unreachable from the binary it is compiled into.
# BOTH project-key derivations — `project_slug` (today) and `sanitize_project_key` (the pre-#2409
# grandfathering rule). `board_state` needs both to match a persisted record against a local hub, and
# needing both is exactly why that module used to be stranded in `src-tauri`.
# A current-thread runtime for the BLOCKING wrappers a sync CLI calls. The async fns above are
# what the app uses directly; the wrappers exist so `bsc` does not need its own runtime story.
# The GitHub REST/GraphQL transport, Tauri-free (`extract-a-tauri-free-github-transport-crate`).
# It lived in `src-tauri/src/github/api.rs` as Tauri commands, which meant `bsc` — a separate
# binary — could not reach GitHub at all, and publish had no path that did not run through a
# React hook. This crate is that transport with the Tauri layer peeled off; the app's commands
# are now thin wrappers over it, so there is ONE implementation rather than two.
# DEPENDENCIES ARE DELIBERATELY MINIMAL. Per CLAUDE.md a crate that pulls DuckDB pays one to two
# minutes of C++ per worktree, so this one takes `bsc-util` for `bsc_base_dir` only and never
# `bsc-data`. `rustls-tls` (not the default native-tls) matches the other CLI-reachable crates
# (cve/research) so the workspace resolves a single TLS backend.
